The things every recruit asks before the summer. Tap a question to open it.
Vivint lines up housing in your summer area, so there’s no apartment hunting and no year-long lease. Most reps live with teammates, which makes carpools and early mornings a lot easier.
Housing is provided for reps in the Direct to Home summer sales program who have an account installed in the preseason. Charges vary depending on your needs. Rent begins on the start date you confirm with the Housing department or the day you arrive in the area (whichever is first), and stops on the end date you confirm or the day you leave (whichever is last). Rent and utilities are deducted weekly from your upfront pay; cleaning and other one-time fees come out of backend pay. Housing isn’t provided for year-round sales, and the full housing policy is sent out before summer starts.

Summer reps work as independent contractors, not employees. Instead of a W‑2, you’ll get a 1099‑NEC at the start of next year showing everything Vivint paid you. That means nothing is withheld from your checks: you’re the one who sets money aside and pays the taxes.
0%

The upside of being your own business: work expenses like your phone, mileage and sales gear can be deductible. Keep receipts and track your miles all summer.
This is general information, not tax advice. Talk to a tax professional about your situation.
In a lot of cases, yes. Many colleges give internship or practicum credit for a summer sales role, especially in business, marketing, communications and entrepreneurship programs. Every school sets its own rules, so start early.
1
Ask your school
Your advisor or career center can tell you what qualifies and when to register, often before the term starts.
2
Get the paperwork
We can confirm your role, your summer dates and a supervisor contact for the forms.
3
Document the summer
Track your hours, training and results. Many programs ask for a reflection paper or a manager evaluation.
You’re paid in two parts: money every week while you’re selling, and a larger payout after the season.
During summer
Upfront, every week
Paid weekly on the accounts you install. Rent and utilities come out of this pay.
After summer
Backend payout
The rest of what you earned, plus bonuses like your rent bonus, paid after the season ends. One-time fees like cleaning come out here.
Your manager will walk you through the exact pay dates and how backend is calculated before summer starts.
The reps who win the summer start before it. Here’s the short list:
Sell in the preseason
An installed preseason account is what qualifies you for housing, and every early sale builds momentum for summer.
Know the products
Learn the lineup in Why Vivint so you can demo it with confidence on day one.
Finish onboarding
Paperwork, background check and any licenses or permits your area requires.
Plan your move
Confirm your start date with Housing, line up your car or travel, and pack for the whole summer.
Save a cushion
Set money aside for the first couple of weeks, plus your 1099 tax savings.
Set your goal
Use the pay scale and Rookie Scenarios to pick a target, then work backward to a daily plan.
Get in shape
You’ll be on your feet for hours. Start building the stamina and habits now.
Still have questions?
Ask your recruiter. That’s what we’re here for.
